Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

associate noun

a partner or colleague

also business associate, partner, business partner, colleague, co-worker, fellow worker

classical

Cic. Rosc. Com. 16: socium fallere quī sē in negōtiō conjūnxit
Traupman 274

socius, sociī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a partner, an associate; in business, a co-partner

Lewis & Short: “fellow, sharer, partner, comrade, companion, associate (very freq. and class.)”; in the language of trade, a partner in business. Feminine socia.

Other words

  • collēga, collēgae m. — a colleague: properly a partner in office

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.144: cum habēret collēgam in praetūrā Sophoclem; Cic. N. D. 1.114 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically one who holds the same office; by extension, an associate in a school or a craft (Lewis & Short).

  • familiāris, familiāris m. — a close friend, an intimate

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.78.1: nōn sōlum hospes meus est, sed etiam … valdē familiāris · Declension on Wiktionary

  • socius operis — fellow worker

    also used · classical · Traupman 314

Examples

  • Aequē enim perfidiōsum et nefārium est fidem frangere quae continet vītam, et pupillum fraudāre quī in tūtēlam pervēnit, et socium fallere quī sē in negōtiō conjūnxit.

    For it is equally treacherous and wicked to break the trust that holds life together, to cheat a ward who has come into one’s care, and to deceive a partner who has joined one in business.Cic. Rosc. Com. 16

  • Bene Periclēs, cum habēret collēgam in praetūrā Sophoclem poētam …

    Pericles did well, when he had the poet Sophocles as his colleague in command …Cic. Off. 1.144

See also member, associate, friend, company.
